findings: New wave-2 template distilled from a recurring field workflow pattern; no prior library source existed.
The field pattern performed external actions (sends, record writes, live clocks) that a public template must not perform.
Field-pattern data was customer-specific and could not be published.

Version 1.1.0 audit against an internal use-case outline for payments operations found three missing steps: the sanctions-alert review queue, the correspondent limit and nostro funding monitor, and customer verification for payments flagged as suspicious.
fixes: Rebuilt the workflow as a single-file, stdlib-only agent with 10 deterministic operations over an invented Woodgrove Bank snapshot.
Replaced every external action with a labeled draft and an explicit no-action gate; removed runtime clocks in favor of a fixed demo calendar.
Used only fictional organizations, people, identifiers, and values; boundary grep against the field-pattern sources returned zero hits.
Added one locked persona-language case and one uploadable skill per operation.

Version 1.1.0 added sanctions_review_queue, correspondent_limits and customer_verification over separate fictional records. They read the screening and fraud monitoring flags as recorded and contain no screening or fraud-detection logic; the analyst decides. The 7 original operations return byte-identical output.
remaining_boundary: Production connections and all external actions require customer approval, least-privilege controls, and an authorized human workflow.
